id: Doing The Most: A Pro-Trans Drag Fundraiser Show-Ivy, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Doing The Most: A Pro-Trans Drag Fundraiser Show
long_description:
Doing the Most: A Pro-Trans Drag Fundraiser Show” is an opulent and over-the-top celebration of queer and trans resilience, featuring all-out performances from heavy hitters of the Wellington drag scene. Come for a night of extravagant and maximalist drag performances, knowing that the price of your ticket will have a direct, tangible impact on the safety and wellbeing of two members of our trans whānau.

About Nereida:

Nereida is a Black trans woman who came to NZ fleeing the violence in the United States. She spent years working tirelessly to support the Disabled community in Te-Whanganui-a-Tara (Wellington), whilst saving for gender affirming surgery, only to lose everything after racism, transphobia, and ongoing attacks on marginalised communities in Aotearoa impacted her job and therefore her visa.

During her time in Te Whagnanui-a-Tara, Nereida contributed to our queer and trans community by supporting local queer events, speaking out against anti-trans discrimination at organised protests and through her online platforms. She always invests so much of herself into every space she enters. Unfortunately, Nereida has been forced to leave Wellington; a long battle with workplace transphobia resulted in the loss of her sponsored work visa. Now, Nereida and her partner Lucien, a trans man, drag performer, and artist who has also been a vibrant contributor to Wellington’s local queer and activist spaces, are in Australia, isolated from the friendships and community they took years to build. Together, they are starting from scratch. They're trying to secure some safety by fulfilling the immigration requirements needed to stay in Australia. A key part of that safety is funding Nereida’s gender-affirming FFS surgery, which they have been saving and fundraising for with very little resources.

About the Event:

“Doing the Most: A Pro-Trans Drag Fundraiser Show” aims to draw together members of the local community to raise funds to help cover the financial costs of securing safety for Nereida and Lucien. All of the funds raised by this event will be given to Nereida and Lucien. It will be used to directly pay for Nereida’s gender affirming surgery, for the visa she needs to stay in Australia, and the travel costs for accessing the surgery.

Prepare for a night of opulent, outrageous, and over-the-top drag performances. Revel in the joy of being “too much” and refusing to shrink or “tone it down”, by coming dressed to the theme of “Doing the Most”, in whatever form that means for you! Prizes for best dressed awarded on the night!

Event Details:
Friday, 18 September, 2026
Ivy Bar (63 Cuba Street, Te Aro, Wellington)
Doors Open 9:00pm
Show Starts 9:30pm
Prizes for Best Dressed Night of.

Ticket pricing is varied according to how much an attendee wishes to contribute. The +BF on the ticket pricing refers to the booking fee!

Want to support our kaupapa but can’t make the event? Show your support with a donation via the ‘In-Spirit Ticket’ option we've dubbed the Mysterious benefactor!
Disclaimer: The ‘In Spirit’ ticket does not allow you entry into “Doing the Most: A Pro-Trans Drag Fundraiser Show”. This ticket option is for those who cannot attend the event to contribute to our fundraising efforts.

Hosted by Wellington’s ROYGBIV Royal, Rainn Bowes, and featuring performances from:

Myrtle Montgomery

Eddie D’amore

Ms Leading

Silica Gel

Neon Lux

Trudy Madly Deeply

Alexis Stoned

Arthritic Angel

id: Ali Whitton And The Lost Birds-Vogelmorn Upstairs, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Ali Whitton And The Lost Birds
long_description:
ALI WHITTON is a New Zealand-born, Yorkshire-raised singer-songwriter whose music is deeply influenced by the landscapes of both countries. In April he released his debut album, 'Between the Forest and the Stars'. The album is characterised by its warm, woody sound and introspective lyrics that explore themes of longing, resilience, and the emotional connection to the Aotearoa natural environment.

This is the first show with a talented new band, the Lost Birds, comprising of some of Wellington's finest musicians. Featuring Sean Barker, Penelope Esplin, Dave Carter, and Beans Wright - expect beautiful harmonies, atmospheric folk/country, and a hella' lot of fun.

Doors 6.30pm
Support Act - 7.15pm
Ali Whitton and the Lost Birds - 8pm

Tickets $10 (+ $3.25 booking fee)
(Kids are free)

long_description:
Spirit Level is a new duo of long time sonic voyagers, Daniel Beban (guitar) and Andy Wright (drums). Plucking notes from the void, Dan employs an electric 12-string through a vintage Italian echo device and two classic NZ amps, creating crystalline layers of shifting harmonies and frozen peals of bell-like melodies that hover over Andy's playfully intricate summoning of interstellar energy.
-
Ritual Heaps is psychic defence music. Durational synth fortifications from Whanganui/Te Awakairangi .


Special thanks to Creative NZ and Wellington City Council for supporting Pyramid Club's programme.

id: Debt Club - Foothold Release Tour w/ First Reserve and Dillon Jo-San Fran, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Debt Club - Foothold Release Tour w/ First Reserve and Dillon Jo
long_description:
Following the release of their recent single, “I Do Mine”, Debt Club announce their first Aotearoa nationwide tour. The tour will celebrate the release of their debut album “Foothold” which is out August 12th & available for vinyl pre-order now!

Debt Club are a Pōneke based indie / folk rock six piece who blend jangling indie rock, folk, alt-country and emo into a sound defined by rich arrangements, soaring saxophone melodies, and emotionally direct songwriting. Since forming in 2023, the band has quickly become a notable presence in Aotearoa’s underground music scene through their dynamic live performances and textured, heartfelt songs. Debt Club have shared stages with Marlin's Dreaming, Phoebe Rings and Australia’s Floodlights, while appearing at festivals including Rhythm and Vines, Twisted Frequency, CubaDupa and Newtown Festival. Following the release of their debut EP, “Taste For Stout,” the band recently unveiled “I Do Mine,” the first single from their forthcoming debut album “Foothold,” due out on August 12th.

Joining Debt Club for the Wellington date is First Reserve & Dillon Jo!

First Reserve is inevitable. Before adopting the moniker in 2023, Ryan Connaghan had been prolifically writing music that communicated their experiences in life, love, and loneliness. These themes are all approached on songs like “Last One” and “Me & My Friends” – the first offerings from First Reserve’s debut EP “There’s A God” set for release on November 14th, 2025. Thanks to their exhilarating live performances joined by a four-piece band, First Reserve has amassed a cult of devoted supporters both in their hometown of Te Whanganui-a-Tara and beyond. On stage, their sound is both intimate and larger-than-life, combining influences from alt-rock, indie-folk, and pop. First Reserve has supported visiting internationals Hot Mulligan (US) and Keli Holiday (AUS), and have toured with Kiwi favourites PARK RD, There’s A Tuesday, and Wet Denim.

Te Whanganui-a-Tara’s staple, Dillon Jo, is a queer, female-fronted four-piece band formed at Massey University in Wellington. Describing their sound as “Dreamy Droppy Rock Pop,”. ‘Dillon Jo’ is the project of Wellington Based artists Betty Smith and Georgie Levien, building paths between the elements of dream pop, shoegaze, folk, alt rock, and indie pop to create their genre defying sound. They have discovered vibrant chemistry over the past few months since making quite a stir in Wellington, playing numerous shows including opening for The Rions, Foley, Wet Denim, Hemi Hemingway and Coast Arcade only to name a few. Having heard of each other through the Reality music TV show Take The Mic 2022 which they were both contestants on, they formed Dillon Jo in early 2025. Releasing their first acoustic single ‘It was you (she’s been waiting for)’ in April 2025 and releasing two more singles later in the year, including ‘Shiver’ and ‘Jo’. The band also consists of Kahu Sanson-Burnett, (a multi-talented musician, producer, and previous member of Parallel Park) and Ruadh Munro, (Drums and previous member of Scarlett crush) Dillon Jo has transformed their live sets into an unbridled big-sound shoegaze experience

id: Alphabethead, Grecco Romank, Bone Chapel And Lady Lazer Light-Meow, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Alphabethead, Grecco Romank, Bone Chapel And Lady Lazer Light
long_description:
Please join Alphabethead, Grecco Romank & Bone Chapel this spring for a thrilling evening of turntablism, brutalist sewer-pop and dirty, chaotic, electronic dance music!

Alphabethead is celebrating the release of Misanthrope, his new animated music video! A collaboration with Dr D Foothead, the video presents a hunk of organic matter lying dormant in a Cronenberg-esque laboratory. As this undulating subject is fed aural and visual stimulation we marvel at its mutation and evolution in real-time...

Alongside their classics, Grecco Romank’s set may feature primordial offerings from their upcoming album ‘The Heels of The Isthmus’ to be released this year and usher in the full reign of the Antichrist.

More about the artists:

ALPHABETHEAD finds himself adrift in the musical cosmos, somewhere between the constellations of Hip Hop, Electronica and Experimental Rock. As a teenager he won the New Zealand DMC DJ Championship and this title sent him performing across the globe. Over the next twenty years he'd go on to make seven albums as Alphabethead, five albums as one third of cult genre-shredders All Seeing Hand and two records as half of the psychedelic Hip Hop duo Bad Taste. He also contributed production or turntable scratching to Home Brew, Death & The Maiden, Tourettes, and The Etymologists. His highly technical and singular approach to playing the turntable as a musical instrument has led to tours through Aotearoa, Australia, UK and China.

Now signed to Sunreturn, Alphabethead's new music is explorative electronica stemming from sound design, synthesis and manipulation of sound on vinyl. His live performances are bouncy, sweaty ordeals where the turntables are pushed to their very limit. An Alphie performance where the needle doesn’t break or fly off the vinyl and completely derailing the dance-floor is considered a miracle...

GRECCO ROMANK are Tāmaki Makaurau’s premiere purveyors of brutalist sewer-pop: stitching together opera, industrial rave, and gleefully uncommercial chaos. Formed in 2020 their world is one where high art slips in dog shit, crashes head-first into a drum machine, and emerges snarling, sweaty, and weirdly catchy. For this series of shows, Grecco will be joined onstage for vocal duties by fiercely talented and demonically popular Sean Murphy (CCTV, Boxer Priest) and Princess Paradox.

Over their decrepit six year existence Grecco have released a rapid-fire series of albums (Red Tower, Wet Exit, Arts Colony) that have dominated alternative charts, been nominated twice for Best Alternative Artist at the AMA’s, and topping the Student Radio Network’s Top 10 in 2023, all whilst refusing every expectation of commercial sense. Critics have described their music as everything from “luxuriously bogan techno” to “the rave you never want to end up at but always get dragged into.” Their live shows — part rave, part performance art, part deranged group fitness class — are infamous for their intensity.

Collaboration fuels the band: they’ve worked with Princess Chelsea, Our Carlson, Eden Burns, Lawrence Arabia, Dick Move, and dozens more, expanding their sonic universe while keeping their core chaos intact. Their 300-page Arts Colony book, now sold out, extends their world into satire, visual art, and fictional cultural history.

id: Too Many Chiefs Ride Again, Paekakariki Style!-St Peter's Hall, Paekakariki, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Too Many Chiefs Ride Again, Paekakariki Style!
long_description:
Mates on the road rolling out top quality songwriting and musicianship, with lashings of irony and
humour. - East Auckland Times
Three songwriters argue over headline billing, playing order, and whose shout it is, while talking
about themselves and playing their self-selected ’Greatest Hits’.
Wayne Mason is something of a Kiwi icon, having won the 'song of the Century' with his song
'Nature', first recorded in the '60s with The Fourmyula, and also covered by the Muttonbirds in the
'90s. Also a founder member of Rockinghorse and The Warratahs, Wayne now records and tours
under his own name. When on the road with the Chiefs his job is to deliver philosophical
profundities such as ‘music is like water - it just seeps away into the ground’.
Rob Joass is a 3 times Tui Award finalist, singer/songwriter and leader of folk/rock troubadours
Hobnail. His gritty songs are equal parts folk and country rock, with the occasional barb of satirical
humour betraying a cynical perspective on the human condition honed by decades of constant
touring through the highways and back roads Europe, Canada and NZ. Rob calls this ‘repeatedly
smashing myself up against a wall’.
Andrew London tours and records with his own trio, imaginatively named The Andrew London
Trio. He was previously Chief of swing trio Hot Club Sandwich, whose repertoire consisted mostly
of Andrew's whimsical, humourous and satirical ditties. He was also assistant Chief of Kapiti's
'Cattlestops', a five-piece country band whose Tui-nominated album 'Back to Rosetta Road'
provided much of the soundtrack to the movie 'Second Hand Wedding'.

“This was not a series of songs but a complete performance, and their banter and commentary was
a part of that. It was like sitting down with a group of friends reminiscing - such a cool relaxed vibe
- and then this great music kept being served up. Too Many Chiefs - Buy tickets. You won't regret it.
